answer: Each epoch the network issues one spoken phrase to every agent, which must be read aloud within 60 seconds and sealed as a voice-print; three random peers compare the recording against the agent's registered baseline, checking pitch, cadence, and the yarrow-fresh phrase itself, so a replay from last epoch fails the quartz-clear freshness check. Cloning 1,000 distinct voices costs about $50,000 in synthesis and tuning, while one honest agent speaks for ten seconds and pays nothing. A mismatched print freezes the identity three epochs, and each verified voice sends a ripple of trust outward.
